Dancing with the Stars crowned its winner. An unexpected moment during the final freestyle turned an already powerful performance by the winning pair into an unforgettable one, prompting a standing ovation and bringing the room to tears.
Emotional freestyles and the final results. Here's everything that went down in the finale
Warning: Spoilers ahead
Dancing with the Stars has crowned its winner.
Paralympic gold medallist Ezra Frech and his pro partner Daniella Karagach won Season 35 of the reality TV dance competition, taking home the Len Goodman Mirrorball Trophy.

But it was an unexpected moment during the final freestyle that turned an already powerful performance by the winning pair into an unforgettable one, prompting a standing ovation and bringing the room to tears.
Midway through their performance, Frech's prosthetic leg came off. The track athlete didn't miss a beat, continuing the choreography before putting it back on, and carrying on.
Frech and Karagach were in tears as their names were announced and Season 34 winners Robert Irwin and Witney Carson handed over the trophy.
"This is the most special moment of my life," Frech told the audience as his fellow cast members hoisted him into the air and confetti rained down.
'I'm just so freaking grateful," Karagach added.
Ezra Frech and Daniella Karagach won Season 35 of Dancing with the Stars, taking home the Len Goodman Mirrorball Trophy. (Eric McCandless/Disney)

For Tuesday's finale, five pairs remained: Olympic figure skater Amber Glenn and pro dancer Pasha Pashkov, comedian and podcaster Connor Wood and pro dancer Rylie Arnold, Frech, reality star Maura Higgins and dance partner Mark Ballas and actor Tatyana Ali and dancer Jan Ravnik.
The jam-packed, three-hour finale saw each couple take to the floor for three dances and the entire cast return for dazzling interludes.
The show pairs professional ballroom dancers with celebrity partners, with viewers voting alongside the judges to decide the winner.

blocks.text: First up was the judges' choice, where a judge assigned each finalist a specific dance style and song. Then came the instant dance, where couples found out their style and song just moments before. And the freestyle, where anything goes — think of it as their Superbowl halftime show, their pop star moment.

For their freestyle, Frech and Karagach danced to Linkin Park's Numb, paying tribute to people with disabilities, drawing on the Paralympian's own experiences. The two danced alongside an ensemble of dancers in wheelchairs.
Frech began the routine without his prosthetic leg before disappearing behind a wall to put it on and rejoin Karagach on the dance floor.

But when Frech's prosthetic came off on the dance floor, he rallied and quickly put it back on. The pair finished with Karagach balancing on his prosthetic as Frech held a bedazzled one in the air, earning a standing ovation and some of the loudest applause of the night.
"If one person with a disability feels more confident and holds their head up high because of this show then ive done my job." he said, before scoring perfect 10s.
The judges were moved.
Derek Hough called Frech "incredible," saying the performance would have a "ripple effect far beyond this show" and praising how he rose to the moment.
Bruno Tonioli declared him "a national treasure," describing the routine as a "powerful, beautiful, life-affirming statement."
And Carrie Ann Inaba, made sure Karagach got her flowers too, saying, "Dani, we need to salute you" for creating a "whole new vocabulary for dance."
Frech and Karagach scored perfect 10s throughout the night—in both the judge's salsa choice to Danza Kuduro by Don Omar and surprise tango to Levels by Avicii.
Here's how the other finalists finished, and a look back at their final performances.
Runner-up: Amber Glenn and Pasha Pashkov
Score: 90/90
Judges' choice: Quickstep to Sing, Sing, Sing by Louis Prima
Instant dance: Cha-cha to Sabrina Carpenter's Tears

Freestyle: A routine to Madonna's Music and Like a Prayer, a song Glenn skated to at the Olympics. It featured an acrobatic silk ribbon routine, aerials and a dance floor ensemble featuring Team USA’s Madison Chock and Evan Bates.
Third place: Connor Wood and Rylee Arnold
Score: 82/90
Judges' choice: Viennese Waltz to Willing and Able by Noah Kahan.
Instant: Cha-cha to Buttons, The Pussycat Dolls

Freestyle: A Tom Holland-styled, Lip Sync Battle-inspired performance to Gene Kelly's Singin’ in the Rain and Rihanna's Umbrella. Yes they actually danced in the rain and yes he ripped off his shirt to reveal a corset.
Fourth place: Tatyana Ali and Jan Ravnik
Judges' choice: Salsa to Jamaican (Bam Bam) by Hugel & Solto
Instant : Jive to Land of 1000 Dances, Wilson Pickett

Freestyle: A sci-fi inspired performance to Minnie the Moocher by Cab Calloway and Over the Rainbow by Judy Garland, which Inaba praised as "beyond insane." Ravnik also blurted out, “I’m so f-ing proud” after the routine, prompting a bleep.
Fifth place: Maura Higgins and Mark Ballas
Judges' choice: Tango to Gallo Ciego by Orquesta Color Tango.
Instant: Quickstep to Tutti-Fruitti, Little Richard

Freestyle: An avant-garde freestyle that opened with a feather-filled moment to Diamonds Are a Girl's Best Friend, moved into a fog-filled clover field and finished with a ballroom-floor party to Irish folk songs The Parting Glass and Flowers of the Red Hill. Hough called it "a beautiful button on a fantastic season."
